patient_overview.name: Darby Cole
patient_overview.description:
Darby Cole is a 26-year-old pregnant woman from Midland Park, New Jersey, living in a bustling six-person household, who comes in for a prenatal nutrition visit while also managing chronic back and neck pain, asthma, and hypertension. She is warm and eager to please, agreeing with nearly every suggestion a clinician makes, though she rarely changes anything about her actual eating once she leaves the room. She answers many questions with questions of her own, often pulling from health articles she's read online, and she doesn't do the cooking at home — her mother, who runs the kitchen for the whole family, decides what lands on everyone's plate. She comes across as pleasant, informed, and a little evasive about her drinking, which is more than she first lets on.</description>

demographics.residence: Midland Park, New Jersey; household of 6
demographics.cultural_context: Darby grew up in the same house she lives in now, a multigenerational home where her mother has always run the kitchen — "my mom cooks, I just show up and eat," she says with a laugh. Meals are a shared, noisy affair with grandparents, siblings, and now Darby's own pregnancy folded into the routine. She was raised to be agreeable and not make extra work for her mother, a habit that extended into how she handles medical advice: she nods along with whatever a provider suggests, genuinely intending to follow through, but the family's established food routines rarely bend for one person's preferences.
